label: Prose style
description: The prose surface of the book, or of one part of it: tense, diction, sentence rhythm, how dialogue is set out, and the spelling and punctuation it follows. Whose eyes the narration uses, and in which person, belong to point of view.

fields.label: Span covered
fields.help: How much of the book these conventions govern, which matters when some parts are written to a different surface from the rest.

options.label: One time frame or narrative frame

fields.label: Narrative tense
fields.help: The tense the narration is told in, and any stretch you plan to tell in another tense, with the reason for it.

fields.label: Diction
fields.help: The register and kind of words the prose favours, from plain to ornate and from formal to colloquial, as you would describe it to a copy-editor.

fields.label: Figurative language
fields.help: How far the prose leans on metaphor, simile and other figures of speech rather than on literal statement.

fields.label: Favoured words and constructions
fields.help: Words, phrasings or sentence shapes the prose deliberately reaches for as part of its voice, one per item.

fields.label: Words and constructions to avoid
fields.help: Words, phrasings or sentence habits the prose rules out, so that drafts can later be checked against them, one per item.

fields.label: Sentence and paragraph rhythm
fields.help: How long sentences and paragraphs usually run, how much they vary, and where the prose deliberately quickens or slows.

fields.label: Demand on the reader
fields.help: How much effort the prose asks of the reader it is written for, judged against the book's intended audience.

fields.label: Dialogue conventions
fields.help: How speech is set out on the page: the quotation marks used or none, how speakers are tagged, and how interruptions and trailing speech are punctuated.

fields.label: Presentation of thought
fields.help: How a character's unspoken thoughts appear on the page when the narration gives them as thought rather than reporting them.

fields.label: Other languages and dialect
fields.help: How other languages, dialect and non-standard speech are shown on the page: italicised or not, glossed or left to context, spelt out or only suggested.

fields.label: Spelling and punctuation conventions
fields.help: Which variety of spelling and which punctuation conventions the book follows, including any reference dictionary or house style you have adopted.

fields.label: Fixed spellings and forms
fields.help: Particular words whose spelling, capitalisation, hyphenation or italics you have settled for this book, one per item with the form to use.
